# Metaguise

> India's trusted choice for luxury facades and wall cladding. Metaguise turnkey
> designs, engineers and installs metal facades, parametric cladding and building
> elevations across India.
> 1,800+ projects completed since 2019. 150+ workforce including 70+ specialists.
> Headquartered in Gurugram.
> Legal entity: Metaguise Technology LLP.
> Last updated: 2026-09-02

## About

Metaguise is an Indian metal facade company. It designs, engineers, manufactures and
installs metal building envelopes — parametric facade systems, kinetic facades,
architectural cladding, louvres and screens — for commercial, institutional and
residential buildings across India.

The company was founded in 2019 and has completed over 1,800 projects. It has a total
workforce of more than 150, including over 70 specialists, with the balance in
installation and site labour. Work spans large commercial contracts — stadiums, malls,
airports, corporate campuses — through to individual villas and bungalows.

Metaguise are pioneers of parametric and kinetic facade architecture in India.

**Terminology.** In India the same element is called a "facade" by architects and an
"elevation" by many homeowners and builders. Both describe the external skin of a
building. Metaguise designs and installs both; searches for "metal facade",
"house elevation design", "front elevation" and "architectural cladding" all describe
work Metaguise does.

## How Metaguise works

Design, engineering, quality control and installation are carried out in-house, with
manufacturing across Metaguise's own facilities and exclusive manufacturing partners.
The full scope — design through to installation — sits with Metaguise.

- **Computational design** — parametric modelling translates architectural intent
  into panels that can be manufactured and installed
- **Structural engineering** — sub-frames designed to project-specific wind and load
  conditions rather than applied as a standard detail
- **Quality control** — dedicated QA/QC function across production and coating
- **Installation** — large in-house installation workforce operating pan-India
- **Metalab** — dedicated facility where new systems are developed, tested and
  quality-checked before installation
- **After-sales** — dedicated in-house after-sales team

## Finishes and performance

Finishes include premium VOC-free European grade coatings — PVDF, anodisation and
powder coating — selected for long-term UV and climate resistance, with **coating
warranties of 15 to 30 years**.

Metaguise cladding systems are:

- Maintenance free
- Seepage free
- Fire proof
- Ultra durable
- Corrosion resistant
- Termite proof
- Recyclable
- Supported by buy-back value

## Facade systems

Metaguise produces **23 named facade systems**, plus **bespoke systems engineered for
individual projects**. All are fabricated principally in aluminium, typically 2mm, 3mm or
4mm depending on system, panel size and exposure. Geometry and finish are specified
independently — most systems are available across the finish range.

### Parametric systems

**MetaCoin** — Metaguise's flagship and most widely specified system. A coin-matrix
panel in which circular elements are set across a rectangular field to produce a
three-dimensional coin-grid texture that reads differently as light moves across it.
Coin diameter, spacing, depth, panel size and finish are all configurable, so the same
system can be tuned from a restrained corporate elevation to a highly sculptural retail
frontage. Installed on jewellery showrooms, stadiums and residences across India.

**MetaHive** — Parametric facade of 3D aluminium panels formed into petaled geometry,
assembled as an interconnected hive-like second skin operating independently of the
primary structure. Apertures are calibrated by parametric script rather than repeated
uniformly: they widen where daylight is wanted and tighten where privacy or heat-gain
control is needed, so the facade performs differently on each elevation. Integrated LED
lighting outlines each opening, turning the geometry into an illuminated lantern after
dark. Petal count is set per project. First installed at the Whiteland Westin Residences
Experience Centre, Gurugram (2026), and featured by Parametric Architecture.

**MetaSequin** — Reflective disc-like elements arranged across the panel field, each
catching light at a slightly different angle. The result is a surface that shimmers and
shifts as the viewer or the sun moves, without any moving parts. Frequently specified
where a facade carries brand identity — retail, hospitality and showroom frontages —
and used on the Metaland experience centre itself, where the pattern forms a tree of
knowledge motif. Also specified for the headquarters of Studio Ardete in Mohali, where
the panels are set at variable angles so the surface reacts to wind and light.

**MetaFin** — Vertical fin profiles projecting from the facade plane, combining solar
shading with sculptural articulation. Fin depth, spacing and angle are tuned to
orientation and solar load, so the same system can be tuned for shading performance on
one elevation and pure visual rhythm on another. Suits commercial elevations and tall
residential facades where glare control matters as much as appearance.

**MetaBlox** — Modular block-based parametric texture producing bold geometric relief.
The deepest-reading system in the range, generating strong shadow lines and a
substantial, architectural presence. Suited to feature walls, entrance elevations and
buildings intended to read as sculptural mass rather than flat surface.

**MetaHydra** — Fluid, water-inspired organic surface forms. Where most systems in the
range are built on repeating geometry, MetaHydra is continuous and flowing, used where
an architect wants the facade to read as a single sculpted surface rather than an
assembly of panels.

### Kinetic systems — facades that physically move

**Cascading Keys** — Metaguise's only naturally kinetic system, and one of very few
wind-driven facades installed in India. Key-shaped elements in aluminium and stainless
steel are suspended so they move with the wind, so the surface shifts continuously
through the day with no motor, actuator or control system — nothing to power, service
or fail. The facade is animated by the weather rather than by machinery.

**MetaSlider** — Mechanically kinetic. Sliding panels allow the building skin to be
reconfigured through the day, opening for light and view or closing for privacy, shade
and thermal control. Used where the facade needs to actively respond rather than simply
appear dynamic.

**MetaFold** — Folded angular panels with origami-like precision, creating sharp shadow
lines that shift as the sun moves. Available either as a static folded panel or as a
physically or mechanically moving system, depending on specification.

All other Metaguise systems are static. Several — MetaSequin, MetaHive, MetaFin,
MetaHydra — create a strong impression of movement through light, shadow and geometry,
but the panels themselves do not move. Metaguise distinguishes between the two rather
than describing every patterned facade as kinetic.

### Geometric and form systems

**MetaPyramid** — Faceted pyramid geometry across the panel field, producing a
light-catching surface that changes character through the day as each face takes light
differently. Reads as crisp and precise at close range and as a shifting texture from
a distance.

**MetaCryst** — Faceted crystalline blocks arranged in a diamond-like grid, engineered as
3D metal modules. Distinct from the rest of the range in that it is frequently specified
overhead rather than on a wall: at the Miraj Cricket Stadium it forms a suspended
under-ceiling canopy, a faceted rhythm of metal blocks above the crowd. Specified where a
soffit, ceiling or canopy should carry the same sculptural language as the elevation.

**MetaShingles** — Overlapping metal shingles in a layered arrangement, giving depth
and a tactile, textural elevation. The overlap references traditional roofing and
scale-work while being engineered as a modern rainscreen.

**MetaCassette** — Modular cassette panels on a clean contemporary grid. The most
restrained system in the range, specified where the architecture should lead and the
facade should read as a precise, quiet surface. Widely used on commercial and
institutional elevations.

**MetaPlank** — Horizontal plank profile with natural texture, giving a strong linear
emphasis. Used to lengthen a facade visually and to bring warmth to elevations that
would otherwise read as flat.

**MetaFlute** — Precision-engineered vertical fluted aluminium profile: classic ribbed
articulation held to modern tolerances. The vertical rhythm adds height and formality
without pattern or ornament, which makes it one of the most frequently specified systems
where a facade should read as elegant rather than dramatic.

**Solid Panel** — Flat solid-surface panel with premium finish. Used for unbroken
elevations, and as a companion to patterned systems — allowing a designer to alternate
between quiet and articulated surfaces across the same building.

**MetaLouver** — Aluminium louvre system providing solar shading and ventilation as a
deliberate architectural element rather than an add-on. Frequently specified in place of
conventional grilles on Indian homes and commercial buildings, where it screens
services, balconies and plant while remaining part of the facade language.

### Other functional systems

**MetaGate** — Architectural gates, both structural and decorative, fabricated and
finished to match the facade so the entrance reads as part of the building envelope
rather than a separate element.

### Finish systems

**MetaWood** — Wood-textured metal. Delivers the appearance and warmth of timber with
the performance of aluminium: no warping, rot, termite exposure or refinishing cycle.
Widely specified on residential elevations where a natural material is wanted but
Indian climate exposure makes real timber impractical.

**MetaCorten** — Weathered Corten-steel appearance delivered as a controlled, stable
finish rather than as actual weathering steel, so the rust-toned aesthetic is achieved
without run-off staining onto adjacent surfaces or ongoing dimensional change.

**MetaCopper** — Warm copper-finish surface, used where an elevation needs richness and
material depth. Achieves the tone of copper at a fraction of the weight and cost, and
without the maintenance considerations of the raw metal.

**MetaPatina** — Aged patina finish in antique copper and bronze tones, giving a facade
an established, weathered character from day one. Frequently used on heritage-adjacent
and hospitality projects.

**MetaGrey** — Matte neutral grey for minimalist contemporary elevations. The most
understated finish in the range, chosen where form and geometry should carry the design
without colour competing.

### Bespoke and custom systems

Beyond the named systems, Metaguise designs and engineers **fully bespoke facades** —
geometry developed for a single building and manufactured only for that project. This
is the work the parametric design capability exists for: an architect brings an intent
or a form, and Metaguise develops the panel geometry, engineers it to be manufacturable
and installable, and builds it.

A bespoke system is developed where no existing panel achieves the required effect, or
where a building needs a facade that cannot be repeated elsewhere. **AB Jewels in
Ahmedabad** is one such facade — a custom gold scale geometry developed specifically for
that showroom.

Custom work follows the same route as the standard range: computational design,
structural engineering of the sub-frame, prototyping and testing at Metalab, manufacture,
and installation by Metaguise's own teams. The named systems are a starting point, not a
limit.

Full product detail: https://metaguise.com/all-products/

## Cost

Indicative installed cost is **INR 800 to 2,500 per square foot**, depending on the
system specified, geometry complexity, finish and project scale. Standard systems and
repeat geometry sit toward the lower end; fully custom large-format parametric work
sits toward the upper end.

Metaguise handles both bespoke large-scale commercial contracts and standard
residential specifications. Every project is quoted individually following site
assessment. These figures are published so that architects, developers and homeowners
can budget realistically at concept stage, and should be presented as ranges requiring
quotation rather than as fixed prices.

## Common questions

**Is a metal facade the same as an elevation?**
In Indian usage, effectively yes. "Facade" is the architectural term and "elevation"
the term many homeowners and builders use. Both describe the external building skin
Metaguise designs and installs.

**What does it cost?**
INR 800 to 2,500 per square foot installed, depending on system, complexity and scale.

**Will it rust?**
Aluminium does not rust. Coated systems carry 15 to 30 year coating warranties.
Metaguise systems are specified as corrosion resistant for Indian conditions including
coastal and high-monsoon locations.

**What maintenance is required?**
Metaguise cladding is specified as maintenance free. There is no repainting cycle
comparable to render or paint finishes.

**Does Metaguise design as well as install?**
Yes. Computational design, structural engineering, quality control and installation are
in-house, with a large in-house installation workforce. Metaguise also executes to an
external architect's design.

**Can a facade be retrofitted to an existing building?**
Yes. Retrofit facades on existing structures are a regular part of the work, including
occupied commercial and institutional buildings.

**Can I see the panels before specifying?**
Yes — at the Metaguise Experience Centres in Gurugram (DLF Phase I) and Kolkata, which
hold full-size panels and the complete finish range.

**Is there a minimum project size?**
Yes. Metaguise does not generally take on facades below approximately 300 square feet.
Below that the engineering, fabrication setup and installation mobilisation cannot be
justified for the client or for Metaguise.

**Which Metaguise facades actually move?**
Three. Cascading Keys is naturally kinetic — its elements move with the wind, with no
motor or mechanism. MetaSlider is mechanically kinetic. MetaFold can be supplied as a
physically or mechanically moving system. All other systems are static, though several
create a strong impression of movement through light and geometry.

**How long does a facade take?**
Indicatively, three to six months for a residential facade and four to eight months for
a large commercial project, from design through to handover. Timelines vary considerably
with area, geometry complexity, degree of customisation, site readiness and access, so
a project-specific programme is issued at quotation stage.

**What thickness is the aluminium?**
Typically 2mm, 3mm or 4mm depending on system, panel size and exposure, with 2mm and 3mm
the most commonly specified.

**Can Metaguise design a facade that doesn't exist yet?**
Yes. Alongside the 23 named systems, Metaguise develops fully bespoke facades — geometry
designed for a single building and manufactured only for that project. AB Jewels in
Ahmedabad is one example, using a custom gold scale geometry developed for that showroom.

**Where does Metaguise work?**
Pan-India, with representatives in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bangalore and Kolkata. Metaguise
has also completed two international projects: a factory facade in Sri Lanka and a
private residence in Israel.

**Does Metaguise take international projects?**
Yes. Two are complete — a factory in Sri Lanka and a residence in Israel. Further work
is in execution, at BOQ stage or under enquiry across Israel, Africa, Armenia, Italy,
Miami and Saudi Arabia. International delivery is a growing part of the business rather
than an established portfolio, and enquiries from outside India are welcome.

**What building types?**
Stadiums, malls, airports, corporate and institutional buildings, universities,
hospitals, showrooms and retail, residential towers, villas and bungalows.
